defect.description: A NETRC path is still expanded under the home directory: os.path.expanduser(f"~/{name}") turns NETRC=/etc/ci/netrc into a path like /home/user//etc/ci/netrc, so a NETRC file outside the home directory (an absolute path, or one starting with ~) is never found and no credentials are returned; only the default NETRC_FILES names should get the ~/ prefix.

review_items: Absolute NETRC paths broken by unconditional ~/ prefix in expanduser (line 17)
Empty-string NETRC resolves to home directory and causes IsADirectoryError
Test only covers bare filename, not absolute-path case
Path traversal via NETRC like ../.secret resolves outside home
votes.evidence_quote: `f"~/{name}"` unconditionally prepends `~/` to the value. When `NETRC="/etc/secrets/netrc"`, this becomes `"~//etc/secrets/netrc"`, which `expanduser` resolves to `$HOME/etc/secrets/netrc` — a non-existent path in the user's home directory. The function returns `None` instead of reading the intended file.
votes.justification: The first finding names the same cause at the same code: the unconditional ~/ prefix in the expanduser call. It also gives the same effect: an absolute NETRC is resolved under home, the file isn't found, and the function returns None.
